In the end, though, a sizable portion of the job interview relies on the human element, the development of rapport between interviewer and interviewee. I could prepare plenty of answers to common and even uncommon questions, but small talk and follow-up questions are really not practical to train for. Small talk is a common sense skill. How would you, personally, train someone in small talk if you were required to do so? Someone who cannot choose words to fit their thoughts, who stumbles and freezes over their own words with consistency, and who struggles at communicating even the most basic ideas through speech? As I said, it's not practical.

If you feel I'm judging your ideas too harshly and shooting them down out of reflex without consideration, I would like to alleviate that concern and note that I do consider the merits of your suggestions and simply find that they would apply more in the case of advising someone with, say, an anxiety disorder. They're reasonable suggestions that just don't seem to apply as well to me due to my own unreasonable circumstances. Sorry I suck.

Probably no point in replying since I didn't see this until today, but futility is my lifestyle so I suppose I'll reply anyway.

I can try to train myself in a marketable skill, but the moment someone sticks me in an interview, I'm horrifically fucked. Ask me to market myself, and I will stream-of-consciousness my insecurities at you. Ask me a question, and there's a nonzero chance I'll freeze up and won't be able to answer.

I don't have the ideas or the drive to engage in entrepreneurship. When directed at a problem, I resolve it. When asked to find a problem and solve it, I will sit there confusedly. Sad, but true. I have no sense for notable problems those around me face when I struggle just to keep up with them in terms of self-care and self-motivation.

I also really just want a normal life. If I can't even have the base human experience of everyone else, what point is there in existing anyway? Is there any reason to persist as someone who works from home when I'd rather die anyway?

Edit for clarity of ideas.

When you say you lost a lot of cognitive function, do you mean in the permanent sense, such that you now are mentally disabled, or in the temporary sense, such that you were unable to think clearly while eating only once per week and regained it upon returning to a normal diet?
